A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D.Va research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and can be reliably aligned, including material relocated in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated control experiments, including policy returns, training time, memory consumption, gradient analyses, and the state-space comparison in Appendix D.1.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds critic and frame-stacking ablations, an ANYmal locomotion demonstration, and additional gradient-norm results.

M1.justification: The decoupled gradient, SHAC-based training, three-frame visual input, privileged-state critic, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The added ablations test variants without revising the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds simulated ANYmal quadruped walking using third-person side-view images. This extends the represented robot embodiments within the existing visual-locomotion domain; Cartpole, Hopper, Ant, and Humanoid remain.

E2.justification: New Figure 14 introduces D.Va without a value function as an explicit ablative comparator. The original DrQ-v2, CURL, DreamerV3, state-to-visual distillation, and SHAC comparisons are retained. Newly cited Xing et al. is discussed but not evaluated.

E3.justification: The added experiments introduce value-function removal and a sweep over one to six stacked input frames. These are new evaluation controls; the original hyperparameters in Tables 2–10 and the retained task definitions and simulation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices D.2–D.3 substantially expand component analysis by testing critic dependence and temporal-input sensitivity across all four original tasks. Appendix D.5 also adds Cartpole and Ant gradient-norm diagnostics alongside the Hopper and Humanoid results already shown in Figure 9.

E5.justification: Checklist item 7 explicitly states that every task and algorithm in Section 4 uses five seeds with mean and standard-deviation reporting. v1 already specified this practice for Figure 4 and five seeds for Figure 13. This broadens the documentation without establishing increased run counts or new statistical tests.

E6.justification: Original result plots and Table 1 values are retained. Added outcomes show poor locomotion learning without the critic, although Cartpole still learns; frame-dependent returns in Table 11; additional gradient curves; and ANYmal learning within 20 minutes. For example, Ant returns are 7218 ± 986.00 with three frames and 9680 ± 222.27 with four. These supplement the original results rather than revise their performance comparisons.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, gradient decomposition, Theorem 1 and its proof, and Appendix A derivation are retained. Changes to mathematical typography do not alter the reasoning or assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and headline claims: renderer-decoupled visual policy learning, computational efficiency, the trajectory-optimization connection, and humanoid learning within four hours with the stated fourfold return improvement.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 qualifies camera-aware behavior from a consistent property to an empirical tendency. Appendix D.3 newly interprets performance as broadly comparable when more than one frame is used. D.2 emphasizes critic dependence, although Figure 14 shows a Cartpole exception. The simulation-quality and real-world-transfer limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Checklist item 5 adds a direct code-repository pointer beyond the project-site link already supplied in v1. The detailed architecture, hyperparameter, rendering, and hardware documentation is otherwise retained. The new pointer does not establish that code was newly released.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hutter et al. (2016) for ANYmal and Xing et al. (2025), with a short discussion of entropy-based stabilization in differentiable reinforcement learning. The broader related-work organization and novelty positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: There are limited prose edits and new appendix cross-references, alongside added experimental subsections, acknowledgments, funding disclosure, and a conference checklist. The affiliation and conference footer also change. The original main-text narrative and section order are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 14–16 and Table 11. The original camera-view Figure 14 is retained as Figure 17, and the original result graphics remain unchanged. Layout reflows around the additions; a small regression removes the Cartpole column heading from Table 1 while retaining its values.

improvement.justification: The critic and frame-stacking ablations provide useful evidence for previously asserted design choices, while ANYmal modestly broadens empirical support. The gains remain limited: ANYmal lacks quantitative baseline comparisons and detailed task-specific settings, and the critic-ablation prose overgeneralizes beyond its Cartpole result. Together with the missing Table 1 heading, these are small drawbacks; the revision nevertheless provides a modest net improvement in evidential support.
